question.problem: Jennifer's marbles are labeled with numbers $7$ through $22.$ If Jennifer chooses a marble at random, what is the probability that the marble number she picks is greater than or equal to $10$ and less than $17?$
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the number on the chosen marble. From the problem statement, we know that $X∼U\{7,8,…,22\},$ and we wish to compute $P(10\le X<17).$

In general, if $X$ follows a discrete uniform distribution over a set $S,$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{|S|}, & x\in S \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have $X∼U\{7,8,…,22\},$ and the set $S=\{7,8,…,22\}$ has $|S|=22-7+1=16$ items. So, we have

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{16}, & x=7,8,…,22 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

In $S,$ the items that satisfy $10\le X<17$ are $10,11,12,13,14,15,16.$ There are $7$ of these elements. Therefore,

$$
P(10\le X<17)=7\cdot \frac{1}{16}=\frac{7}{16}.
$$
